Oral medicine and dentistry · published research

Denture stomatitis

Small clinical studies report changes in fungal or inflammatory outcomes, but a combined photodynamic-therapy and PBM comparison had lower resolution than miconazole alone.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Small clinical studies report changes in fungal or inflammatory outcomes, but a combined photodynamic-therapy and PBM comparison had lower resolution than miconazole alone.

Summary of the Evidence

Five human records are listed: four comparative clinical reports (two randomized trials and two other controlled comparisons) and one two-case series. Interventions and outcome measures differ; one comparison combines antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) with PBM, so reports do not represent a uniform PBM intervention. No animal or in-vitro/ex-vivo study is listed.

Human and clinical evidence

The older studies report changes in fungal growth, inflammatory markers or mucosal healing. In a 40-participant comparison, miconazole had a higher cure rate than methylene-blue aPDT followed by LLLT (80% versus 40%); because aPDT was combined with PBM, the PBM contribution cannot be isolated (Maciel et al. 2015). Small samples and dated protocols limit certainty (Maver-Biscanin et al. 2004, 2005; Simunović-Soskić et al., 2010). These records evaluate different questions—antifungal activity, cytokines, mucosal lesions, or adjunctive symptom control—and follow-up is generally short. The two randomized titles should therefore not be pooled as if they tested the same intervention or endpoint. None demonstrates prevention of recurrence after denture adjustment or provides a precise adverse-event estimate.

Primary original studies: Maver-Biscanin et al. 2004 Maciel et al. 2015

Animal evidence

none identified.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

none identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Maver-Biscanin et al. compared 685 nm visible red and 830 nm near-infrared diode protocols; the record reports 3 J/cm² and treatment on 5 days for the study regimen. Maciel et al. combined methylene-blue photodynamic inactivation with low-level laser treatment. These are distinct interventions and cannot be treated as a single PBM dose.

Interpretation

The studies test different questions and their outcomes are not interchangeable. The 40 percent resolution in the combined arm versus 80 percent with miconazole does not identify the effect of PBM because photodynamic treatment was also used. The evidence does not establish comparative recurrence prevention or a standardized adjunctive regimen.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low. Small studies use different protocols, and one combines PBM with antimicrobial photodynamic therapy.
Publications and records5 unique titles.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Five human reports evaluate differing endpoints such as fungal growth, inflammatory markers, mucosal healing, and combined treatment. In a comparison with miconazole, the methylene-blue photodynamic-therapy plus PBM arm had a lower resolution rate. Small samples and mixed interventions prevent a confident estimate of PBM's independent contribution.
